prose: Scott Werner tells a fable: a Tokyo restaurant where the owner, tired of explaining his grandmother's miso soup, built machines that cook everything perfectly. The chefs revolted - where's the art, the soul, the training? - so he turned them into inventors instead: flavor architects and experience designers creating dishes the machines can't make yet.

The restaurant now has a three-year waiting list, and the owner's line is the thesis: 'We forgot how to cook, so we could remember how to create.' Applied to the AI moment, the only skill that matters is the one machines can't supply - imagining what doesn't exist yet.
highlights: Fable: the Tokyo restaurant with no cooks, only machines
Chefs became inventors - flavor architects, experience designers
Three-year waiting list; every meal is something that didn't exist yesterday
Thesis: 'We forgot how to cook, so we could remember how to create'
The only skill that matters now: imagining what machines can't yet make
